items.markingKey: (a) ∫ from 0 to 6 of v dt (M1) = 12 (A1). (b) v = 0 at t = 2 (A1); split the integral and take moduli (M1); 20 m (A1).

items.stem: A boat cuts its engine and drifts; its velocity is v = 24e^(−0.19t) m s⁻¹. Find the time taken for the velocity to halve, and the distance travelled in that time.
"If a(t) < 0 the particle is moving backwards." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.answer: Negative acceleration means v is decreasing; the particle moves backwards only if v < 0.
items.markingKey: Negative acceleration means v is decreasing; the particle moves backwards only if v < 0. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: The velocity of a particle is v(t) = 2.0cos(0.8t) + 0.5 m s⁻¹, 0 ≤ t ≤ 4. Find (a) the displacement of the particle from its initial position at t = 4 (b) the total distance travelled.
A particle oscillates so that its displacement is s = 6cos(t) cm at time t seconds. Find the maximum speed of the particle.
items.markingKey: v = −6sin(t) (M1 A1); max |v| = 6 (A1).

items.stem: The acceleration of a particle is a(t) = 3t − 1 m s⁻². When t = 0 its velocity is 3 m s⁻¹ and its displacement from O is −3 m. Find its displacement when t = 2.

A particle moves along a line with velocity v = t² − 9t + 20 m s⁻¹ for t ≥ 0. Initially it is −1 m from O.
(a) Find the times at which the particle changes direction.
(b) Find an expression for the displacement s(t).
(c) Find the total distance travelled in the first 6 seconds.
(d) Find the displacement from the start at t = 6.
items.markingKey: (a) v = 0 (M1) A1 (b) integrate (M1) A1; constant (A1) (c) split at turning points (M1) A1 A1 (d) A1 [Total 9 marks]

items.stem:
A sledge leaves the point O at 11 m s⁻¹; its acceleration t seconds later is a = −2e^(t/2) m s⁻².
(a) Show that v(t) = 15 − 4e^(t/2).
(b) Find the exact time at which the particle comes to instantaneous rest.
(c) Find the displacement from O at that time.
(d) Explain why the particle is slowing down for 0 < t < T, where T is the time found above.

items.stem:

items.stem: Given v(t), displacement from t = 0 to t = T is
options: ∫ from 0 to T of v(t) dt
items.answer: ∫ from 0 to T of v(t) dt
items.markingKey: C. Displacement is the integral of velocity.

items.stem: A runner jogs 4 km east and then 5 km west along a straight road. What are her distance travelled and displacement?
items.markingKey: C. Distance adds the lengths; displacement is the net change.

items.stem: If s = 3 sin(2t), the maximum speed is
items.markingKey: 6. v = 6 cos 2t, max |v| = 6.

items.stem: A particle has displacement s = −2t³ − 6t² − 4t + 4 m at time t s. Determine whether the particle is speeding up or slowing down at t = 2, explaining your reasoning.
items.markingKey: v(2) = −52 (A1); a(2) = −36 (A1); same sign so the speed is increasing (R1).

items.stem: Explain why ∫ v dt and ∫ |v| dt give different results if the particle changes direction.
items.answer: When v < 0 the integral of v subtracts that part of the motion, whereas |v| counts it as positive distance.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: When v < 0 the integral of v subtracts that part of the motion, whereas |v| counts it as positive distance. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: A particle has displacement s = 3 sin(5t). Explain why its acceleration is always directed towards O and find where its speed is greatest.
items.markingKey: v = 15 cos(5t), a = −75 sin(5t) = −25s (M1 A1); opposite sign to s so towards O (R1); |v| max = 15 when sin(5t) = 0, i.e. at O (A1).

items.stem: A particle has displacement s = 3t³ + 2t² − 4t + 2 m at time t s. Determine whether the particle is speeding up or slowing down at t = 5, explaining your reasoning.
items.markingKey: v(5) = 241 (A1); a(5) = 94 (A1); same sign so the speed is increasing (R1).

items.stem: Felix says that a particle with velocity v = t − 4 m s⁻¹ travels 15/2 m between t = 0 and t = 5, because ∫ from 0 to 5 of v dt = −15/2. Explain the error and find the actual distance travelled.
items.markingKey: v changes sign at t = 4, so the particle changes direction (R1); the integral of v gives net displacement, not distance (R1); distance = ∫|v| dt = 17/2 m (M1 A1).

items.stem: A particle has displacement s = 7 sin(5t). Explain why its acceleration is always directed towards O and find where its speed is greatest.
items.markingKey: v = 35 cos(5t), a = −175 sin(5t) = −25s (M1 A1); opposite sign to s so towards O (R1); |v| max = 35 when sin(5t) = 0, i.e. at O (A1).

items.stem: A particle moves in a straight line so that its displacement from O after t seconds is s = 2t³ − 30t² + 144t + 1 metres, t ≥ 0. Find the velocity of the particle when t = 0, and state its direction of motion.
items.answer: 144 m s⁻¹, moving in the positive direction
items.markingKey: v = ds/dt = 6t² − 60t + 144 (M1 A1); v(0) = 144 (A1); direction from the sign (R1).

items.stem: "If v = 4e^(−t) then the distance travelled up to t = 10 is 4e^(−10)." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.markingKey: Integrate: 4(1 − e^(−10)) ≈ 4.00 m. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.
